clue.text: Fool in island stream, short in distance

indicators.note: in says the shortened stream sits inside the word for distance

parts.note: a mile is a unit of distance

indicators.note: short means the last letter of the word for stream is cut off

parts.note: a beck is a small stream in northern English dialect

explanation.surface: Reads like a muddled travel note about an island, a stream and how far away they are.
explanation.walkthrough: A beck is a northern English dialect word for a stream; 'short' drops its last letter, and 'in' puts the result inside the distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a stupid person; the noun is a common insult.

clue.text: Part of foot kept by Darwin (Charles)

indicators.note: kept by says the answer is held within the letters of the name that follows

explanation.surface: A detail of anatomy preserved by the famous naturalist, perhaps in a specimen jar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept by' points at letters held inside Darwin Charles, spanning the end of one name and the start of the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A foot as a length is made up of twelve smaller units, each one part of it.

clue.text: Lolita hobbles badly in company of dancers

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of the preceding words are put together wrongly, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl called Lolita limps clumsily while dancing with a troupe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bolshoi is Moscow's renowned ballet troupe, a company of professional dancers.

clue.text: Hit on the bonce with teacher's ruler

parts.note: bonce is British slang for head; to crown someone is to hit them on the head
a head is the head teacher of a school

explanation.surface: A pupil gets struck on the head with the teacher's wooden ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bonce' is British slang for the head, and 'crowned' in slang means hit on the head; HEAD is the head teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch who has been crowned is a sovereign, so a ruler of a kingdom.

clue.text: Slowly stocking a type of shed

indicators.note: stocking means holding something within, so the word for slowly takes in the letter

parts.note: lento is the musical direction meaning slowly

explanation.surface: Someone is slowly filling a shed with supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: LENTO is the Italian musical term for slow; 'stocking' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a simple shed built against a wall, with a sloping roof.

clue.text: Circulate plans for junk mail

indicators.note: circulate suggests going round, so the word for plans is turned back to front

explanation.surface: An instruction to send out plans as unwanted bulk mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circulate' is read as turning round: MAPS reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsolicited bulk email is called this, after a tinned meat brand and a Monty Python sketch.

clue.text: Hairstyle fixed with roller

parts.note: a roller is a long sea wave

explanation.surface: A hairdo set in place using a curler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roller' looks like a hair curler, but here it is a big breaking wave at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A perm is a chemical treatment setting curls or waves in the hair for months.

clue.text: Very old mead — vile, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things went wrong, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sad verdict on an ancient batch of honey wine that tastes horrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Something from the Middle Ages is centuries old, so very old in casual use.

clue.text: Instrument in small room close to piano

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery

indicators.note: close to means the closing letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A musical instrument kept in a tiny room next to the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' looks like 'near', but it means the end letter of piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A cello is a large bowed string instrument played between the knees.

clue.text: Changed, or stumbled, heading off

indicators.note: heading off means the front letter of the word for stumbled is removed

parts.note: faltered means stumbled or lost momentum

explanation.surface: Asks whether someone changed course or just tripped on the way out.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something that has been modified or made different.

clue.text: Reason for not making it to court, perhaps

definitions.text: Reason for not making it to court, perhaps

parts.words: Reason for not making it to court, perhaps
parts.note: court suggests a law court and a missed hearing, but it is a tennis court, and the injury keeps a player off it

explanation.walkthrough: 'court' suggests a missed day in a law court; the court meant is a tennis court, and this arm injury could keep a player off it.
explanation.definitionFit: The painful elbow condition named after the sport could stop a player from getting to the court.

clue.text: Cloth in one, a woven fabric

indicators.note: woven means interlaced, so the letters of the preceding words are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Describes a single woven fabric made from cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: HONITON is a town in Devon, England, famous for its lace.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a delicate bobbin lace made in Devon, so a kind of fabric.

clue.text: Changes on-off devices

definitions.meaning: ... as a verb means changes or swaps
... as a noun are controls that turn power on or off

explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb meaning swaps and as a plural noun for electrical controls.

clue.text: Queer fish in dam do

parts.note: a weir is a low dam across a river

explanation.surface: An odd character turns up at a party held at a dam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do' is a party, but here it simply supplies its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A queer fish is an old idiom for an odd, eccentric person.

clue.text: Big screen forming part of rhetoric in emails

indicators.note: forming part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A large display screen used to show off persuasive wording in emails.
explanation.definitionFit: The big screen is an idiom for films shown in picture houses, as opposed to television.

clue.text: Study involving some ravine

indicators.note: involving means wrapping around, so the word for study surrounds the word for some

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
any can mean some, as in 'have you any?'

explanation.surface: A field study that takes in part of a gorge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'con' meaning to study or learn by heart is an old usage, common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A canyon is a deep gorge, so a large ravine.

clue.text: One arranging breaks in great Levant resort

indicators.note: resort is read as re-sort, sorting the letters again into a new order

explanation.surface: A holiday organiser at a fine resort in the eastern Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday spot but is read as re-sort, the signal to rearrange; 'breaks' are holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who books holidays for clients arranges their breaks.

clue.text: Stud manager

definitions.meaning: a stud is a raised knob or ornament on a surface
the person in charge at work

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a decorative knob, like a stud, and the person who runs things.

clue.text: Aid distributed during religious festival

indicators.note: during means the shuffled letters come within the word for religious
distributed means spread around, so the letters of aid are rearranged

explanation.surface: Aid is handed out over a religious festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'religious festival' reads as one phrase, but 'religious' supplies its own word; 'distributed' rearranges the letters of aid, and 'during' places them inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday was originally a holy day, a feast or festival day.

clue.text: Embargo absorbing English leader of overseas party

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the word for embargo holds the letter

parts.note: a ban is an embargo or prohibition

indicators.note: leader of means the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A trade ban that draws in the English head of an overseas political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' looks political, but a beano is British slang for a lively party or knees-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Beano is informal British slang for a celebration or jolly outing.

clue.text: Location in view? Sounds like it

indicators.note: sounds like it says the answer is a word pronounced the same as the word for view

parts.note: a sight is a view or something seen

explanation.surface: Asks whether a place within sight is spoken the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a place or position where something is located.

clue.text: We pass on processed vegetables

indicators.note: processed means worked over, so the letters of the preceding words are put in a new order

explanation.definitionFit: Snow peas, or mangetout, are flat edible pea pods eaten as a vegetable.
